paper.title: weekly-skill: layout-aware PDF structure parser for scientific papers (阅读01｜文献文档解析)
paper.authors: skill submission; demo papers parsed: Kaiming He et al. (arXiv:1512.03385); Ashish Vaswani et al. (arXiv:1706.03762); Jacob Devlin et al. (arXiv:1810.04805); Tom B. Brown et al. (arXiv:2005.14165); Alexey Dosovitskiy et al. (arXiv:2010.11929, the held-out sample)
target_claims: A skill that turns a scientific PDF into a page- and bbox-traceable structured document (blocks, sections, tables, figures, formulas, references) in one deterministic pass, and reports character-level completeness instead of asserting it.

artifacts.description: ResNet (two-column CVPR) parse report: per-page column count and gutters, type histogram, char_recall, selfcheck.
Reading-order text for ResNet; every block carries its page, type, column and bbox in an HTML comment.
ResNet architecture table rebuilt cell-by-cell from word boxes (7 columns, nested multi-line cells preserved).
Figure 2 crop with caption glued to its artwork.
Layout diagnosis overlay: box colour = block type, magenta = detected gutter, numbers = reading order.
Reading-order text for the single-column paper.

Bare-agent baseline vs this skill on the same five PDFs: running-header lines, figure-label chars in body, glued headings, cross-column interleavings, tables/cells, blocks with bbox (per case and per page).
Held-out sample (ViT, ICLR template): 22 pages, single-column body + two-column appendix, 742 blocks, 22 sections, selfcheck ok.
Measurement script behind A13: recomputes every baseline metric from the PDF geometry.
One-screen paste-and-use contract for an agent (install, three commands, what to read, what to report, three rules).
Baseline method, metric definitions, per-corpus table and the caveats (n/a is n/a).
27 black-box assertions over three synthetic fixtures (CJK two-column, multi-line title, scanned page); no pytest, no network, exit 1 on failure.
Trimmed doc.json from the same run: 12 pages, 16 sections, page-1 blocks, T1 cells and bbox_cells (63 each) - the artifact behind the bbox/table claims.
Deterministic generator for the three fixtures, so the tests can be rebuilt from source.

expected_outputs.name: char_recall_resnet
expected_outputs.reference: emitted_chars / (text_layer_chars - dropped_running_chars) for the two-column paper

expected_outputs.name: char_recall_transformer
expected_outputs.reference: same completeness metric for the single-column paper

handoff.next_suggestion: widen the envelope: 3-column layouts, fully scanned books, and tables without ruling lines are declared-but-untested; run the OCR branch end-to-end with a vision model on a real scan
handoff.hypothesis: the remaining error budget is dominated by column detection on pages where a full-width figure splits a multi-column band

next_owner_hint.start_at: references/method.md section 7 (reading order) and section 4 (column voting)
next_owner_hint.why: the residual error budget sits in pages where a full-width figure splits a multi-column band

modality_notes.execution: results/ holds a real run of the bundled parser on five public papers; results/run.log is the verbatim stdout of that run; results/baseline.json is the bare-agent comparison; tests/test_engine.py exercises the CJK, multi-line-title and scanned-page paths without needing the corpus
modality_notes.characterization: 7 deviations from paper, 10 envelope entries (7 measured / 3 declared), 5 failure modes, 4 sensitivity sweeps, plus 3 synthetic fixtures (CJK two-column, multi-line title, scanned page)
